messages:
maya: Quick sync — we need to nail sampling for A/B canary comparisons. Runtime ingest costs spiked last week when a couple teams did full-traffic diffs. Proposal: sample ~10% of requests for trace-level telemetry (latency histograms, streaming token latencies, kv-cache samples) and keep 100% exact aggregates/counters. Thoughts? :wave:

ben: Agree we need sampling. Curious what 'trace-level telemetry' covers — is that p95/p99 + per-request token timelines + cache-hit traces?

cassandra: Trace-level = latency hist (p50/p90/p95/p99), streaming token-by-token latencies (only for sampled traces), and a tiny fraction of kv-cache hit logs. Token logs are the expensive bit.

liam: Observability ask: 10% traces is still sizable for high-volume routes. We should do stratified sampling by route and model size. High-volume routes (e.g. /embed, short-gen) should default to 1% or even 0.1%.

zoe: Quota/legal note: Dedicated customers require exact request counters for billing/usage exports. Sampling can only affect traces, not aggregates. So counters must be exact and derived before sampling.

maya: Agreed — counters exact, traces sampled. Draft config idea (example):

```yaml
sampling:
  traces:
    default: 0.10
    route_overrides:
      /embed: 0.01
      /chat: 0.05
    model_overrides:
      rdx-13b: 0.05
  counters: exact
```

ben: How will this interact with the canary compare dashboard? To get valid diffs we need comparable sample sets between control and variant. Suggest deterministic bucketing by request_id hash + rollout seed so the same user/request goes to the same sample bucket across variants.

cassandra: Yes — deterministic bucketing is the only sane way. Runtime can compute `hash(request_id, rollout_seed) % 100` and compare to sampling thresholds. We should surface a header `X-compare-bucket` so downstream systems can correlate.

liam: Dashboard side: if buckets are stable we can compute pairwise diffs and p-values. We also need a metric for sampled counts per bucket so we can compute effective N for each comparison. Can you emit `telemetry.sampled_count` with `{route,model,bucket}` labels?

zoe: We can emit `telemetry.sampled_count{route,model,bucket}` but must cap bucket cardinality. Use boolean or up to 10 bins (0-9) to keep cardinality low.

maya: OK — plan: deterministic buckets (10 bins), exact counters always emitted, sampled traces tagged with bucket label. Add sampled_count metric so dashboards know effective sample size. Also need an onboarding checklist for teams adding new routes: expected sample rate, whether token logs required, and a rough cost estimate. I'll draft a template.

ben: +1. One ops request: allow a fast, temporary override to increase sampling for debugging without a full deploy. E.g. runtime respects `X-force-sample: 1` for a short window, and we log who triggered it.

deploy-bot: deploy: feature-flag "canary-sampler" enabled in staging.

maya: Next steps: ben -> PR for config schema and route/model override semantics; cassandra -> implement deterministic bucket + `X-compare-bucket` header; liam -> add sampled_count panel and CI assertion for minimum N; zoe -> confirm metric naming and bucket cardinality cap; I'll circulate the onboarding checklist doc. Ping me if you hit blockers.

ben: working on the schema PR today.

cassandra: on it, will open an RFC for header format.

liam: will add panels and a small test harness for p-value sanity checks.

zoe: confirming metric naming with infra telemetry team, will update here.

maya: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
